item.title: Build a workflow
item.description:
Workflows are a Pro page for a sequence you run again. First enable Settings → Experimental → Workflows; it is off by default. A block runs code, a code file, a saved HTTP endpoint, an MCP tool, or an OpenAI-compatible model. A decision picks one branch. A loop repeats a frame. The same file is the page and the YAML.

This is separate from a collection runbook, a Markdown runbook, and a repo runbook. Those stay as they are.

item.title: Capture a session as a Workflow
item.description:
Pro — Capturing a session as a Workflow is a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

Use Capture session from the @ command list, type @capture, or press Ctrl+Alt+R (Ctrl+Shift+R is an alternate on Windows and Linux where AltGr occupies Ctrl+Alt; macOS uses Cmd+Option+R). Capture is Pro and applies to the current tab. Ask the AI in the prompt, run a shell command, call a saved endpoint, or call an MCP tool as usual. Start capture before the actions you want to include.

item.title: Node types and code languages
item.description:
A node on the canvas is a block in workflow YAML. Workflows are Pro and must be enabled under Settings → Experimental → Workflows. Choose the smallest block that does the job: an HTTP block for a saved endpoint, an MCP block for a saved tool, and code for a transformation that needs programming. Use AI when the task needs model judgement rather than a fixed rule.

Node types at a glance link

Editor name YAML kind Purpose When to use it
Code code Execute an inline snippet in one of seven languages. Validate input, reshape JSON, calculate a value, or adapt one service’s output for another.
Code file code_file Read a local source file and execute it with the same code runner. Keep a larger script in source control or reuse it across workflows.
Git file git The editor describes a source file in a public repository. Not currently runnable. Use Code file with a reviewed local checkout until Git file execution is implemented.
HTTP endpoint http Call a saved HTTP endpoint, or a local mock:// example. Reuse configured API connections and credentials without writing an HTTP client.
MCP tool mcp Connect to a saved MCP server and call a named tool. Use a tool’s published contract and existing transport/authentication settings.
AI ai Send a system message and prompt to a saved OpenAI-compatible model connection. Summarise, classify, or interpret information that a deterministic comparison cannot handle.
Decision decision Evaluate conditions and route to one target block. Branch on a status, count, threshold, or the presence of a value.
Loop loop Execute nested body blocks for each item, a fixed count, or while a condition holds. Process a list or repeat bounded work without copying blocks.

The editor currently offers eight types; the runner accepts the seven types other than git. A trigger starts a workflow and is configured on Triggers. It is not another runnable block type.

item.title: Code and block examples
item.description:

These examples use the input and output contract. TERMORQ_INPUT contains a path. Read that file; do not parse the environment variable itself as JSON. The code runs locally, so install the language runtime listed in Node types and code languages.

item.title: Triggers, runs, and notices
item.description:
Pro — Workflows, including their triggers and runs, are a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

A workflow runs when you press Run, or when its selected automatic trigger fires. Choose one automatic trigger in Triggers. Switching types keeps each type’s saved settings, but only the selected type starts automatic runs. Older workflows with several configured triggers keep their settings when you choose which one is active. Manual runs stay available in the editor. Triggers run only while Termorq is open. A missed schedule is not replayed. One workflow has one active run. A second start is recorded as Skipped · already running. Two workflows may run at once.
